Sinovation Ventures is a Beijing-based technology venture investor founded in 2009, managing over US$3 billion across ten funds and more than 500 portfolio companies.

The data is a firm profile, not an infrastructure record. It establishes scale of capital and deal count, which is the upstream layer that eventually funds compute, data centers, and power procurement. A venture firm of this size in China sits close to the hardware and semiconductor supply chain that AI scaling depends on, but the record does not name a single portfolio company, so no specific link to chips, buildings, or grid capacity can be drawn from it.

What the data does not cover is as important as what it does. There are no cases, no products, no lawsuits, no SEC filings, and no patents. The founding is attributed to a team led by Dr. Kai-Fu Lee, and the asset and portfolio figures are the firm's own description of itself rather than independently verified counts.

For AI specifically, this entry tells a reader that a large Chinese technology investor exists and has been deploying capital since 2009. It does not say where that capital went, whether any of it reached AI infrastructure, or how it compares to peers. Any claim about Sinovation's role in the compute buildout would have to come from data not present here.
